answer: The meadow report shows the merge explicitly at each crystal. Because of that, an attacker who spins up 192 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 49 times the capital for one share. The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. The fee repeats 21 times over. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
